title: Model Manifest
description: Per-model manifest declaring identity, inputs, outputs, UQ contract, invocation, lineage, and discoverability metadata. Co-located with the model executable and a sibling model_card.md. Validated when the package is loaded (opencontractml.manifest).

id.description: Stable identifier; used in URLs, run records, and registry keys. Lowercase ASCII, must start with a letter.

name.description: Human-readable name, for display in listings and reports.

spec_version.description: Manifest-spec (schema) version this model is authored against, as MAJOR.MINOR. Optional and additive; an absent value is treated as "1.0" (the v1 spec). A consumer loads any manifest whose MAJOR is <= its supported maximum (minor bumps are additive and back-compatible) and rejects a higher MAJOR loud at load (back-compat policy). Distinct from `version`, which is the model's own semver.

contact.description: Contact for the team (email or chat handle).

domain.description: Engineering domain (e.g., thermomechanical_fatigue, vibration, flow). Usable as a browse or filter facet.

modality.description: Coarse input-to-output shape. Usable as a browse or filter facet.

tags.description: Free-form tags, for filtering and search.

analysis_type.description: Plain-language analysis category for non-expert discovery (e.g. "fatigue life", "vibration response", "flow rate"). Optional and additive. Free text, like `domain` and `tags` — NOT a fixed vocabulary. Phrase it the way a non-CAE/ML user with an analysis in mind would.

purpose.description: One-line statement, in plain language a non-CAE/ML reader can understand, of what the model predicts.

when_to_use.description: Plain-language guidance on appropriate use cases, written for a non-expert who has an analysis in mind. An empty value draws an advisory warning from the package validator (never a rejection).

when_not_to_use.description: Plain-language guidance on inappropriate use cases. Surfaced in reports.

primary_inputs.description: Input names to show first wherever runs of this model are listed (for example, as default columns).

primary_outputs.description: Output names to show first wherever runs of this model are listed (for example, as default columns).

executable.description: Path to the model executable, relative to the manifest file.

timeout_s.description: Hard timeout, in seconds, after which the consumer stops the executable and records an error.

batch_supported.description: If true, the executable accepts mode=batch and emits one JSON output per input row.

training_data_version.description: Identifier or version tag for the training dataset.

training_date.description: ISO-8601 date the model was trained.

metrics.description: Free-form map of metric_name -> value. At least one metric required.

retrain_cadence.description: Free-form description of retrain schedule (e.g., quarterly, on-demand).

model_card.description: Path to the model card markdown file, relative to the manifest file. Required; validated when the package is loaded (front-matter plus the 11 mandatory H2 sections, in order).

examples.description: Ready-made input sets a consumer can offer as examples to run.

name.description: Field key the entrypoint reads from its stdin JSON. Starts with a lowercase letter; after that, letters of either case, digits and underscores. The uppercase tail is deliberate: unit suffixes carry case (peak_temp_K is kelvin, peak_temp_k is kilo), so a lowercase-only rule would reject the name that says which. Every name the lowercase-only pattern accepted is still accepted.

units.description: Display units: the units a person enters and reads the value in. A consumer may offer compatible alternatives.

canonical_units.description: Units the executable expects. A consumer converts a value from display units to canonical units before sending it.

range.description: [min, max] in canonical units. A value outside the range is a warning, not a refusal.

file_kind.description: Required for type=file: the file format the input accepts.

default.description: A suggested value a consumer may pre-fill.

viewer.description: How a consumer should present this output. field_contour is accepted but deferred: opencontractml.manifest.deferred_viewer_outputs lists the outputs that use it, so a consumer can flag them instead of rendering them wrongly.

form.description: Default UQ form. Per-output blocks may override.

per_output.description: Map from output field name to its UQ field declarations. Must cover every output.

empirical_coverage.description: Achieved coverage on the holdout set.

expected_hint.description: Optional plain-language hint about the result the example should give.
